headline: OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT voice with real-time, interruptible conversations
summary: The new GPT-Live-1 model allows ChatGPT to speak and listen simultaneously, making interactions more natural and responsive. It also supports real-time translation.
details: OpenAI has overhauled ChatGPT's voice mode with its new GPT-Live-1 model, aiming for interactions that feel more like conversing with another person. This advanced model can speak and listen concurrently, reducing interruptions and allowing for more fluid dialogue.

GPT-Live-1 is described as OpenAI's "smartest voice model" yet. It intelligently routes queries to its most capable text models, such as GPT-5.5, for complex reasoning or web searches, enabling faster transitions from research to discussion.

The new model enhances conversational flow by supplementing discussions with AI-generated visuals, such as sports scores or weather forecasts. This moves beyond the previous turn-based model, which often struggled with natural conversation.

A key advancement is the "full duplex" capability, allowing ChatGPT to process input and produce output streams continuously and simultaneously. This enables features like real-time translation, where the AI translates speech as it's being spoken.

Users can now instruct ChatGPT Voice to pause and wait for their prompt, a feature previously unavailable. The AI also provides verbal cues like "mhmm" and "got it" to acknowledge it's actively listening.

OpenAI has implemented safeguards to prevent harmful responses and can end chats in high-risk situations. The model is also trained to offer crisis helpline support for self-harm discussions and provide age-appropriate responses for younger users.
GPT-Live-1 is rolling out on iOS, Android, and the web for Go, Plus, and Pro subscribers. Free users will have access to a more efficient version, GPT-Live-mini-1.

headline_marked: Google Photos [[Video Remix]] uses Gemini Omni for AI editing
headline: Google Photos Video Remix uses Gemini Omni for AI editing
summary: Transform your videos with AI filters, lighting changes, and background swaps. Rolling out now for AI subscribers.
details: Google is rolling out a new feature called Video Remix to Google Photos, allowing users to edit and transform their saved videos using AI. This feature is powered by Gemini Omni, Google's advanced AI model capable of creating content from various inputs.

Video Remix simplifies video editing by offering templates within the 'Create' tab of Google Photos. Users can apply effects like watercolor filters, adjust lighting to simulate a morning glow, or even change the video's background, all processed in seconds.

Gemini Omni, announced in May, is designed to be more intuitive and realistic than previous models. It understands physical forces and accepts a wider range of inputs, enabling more lifelike scene generation. It also supports inserting users into videos via digital avatars, watermarked by Google's SynthID tool.

The Video Remix feature is now available to Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers in the US and select countries. This move signifies Google's ongoing integration of generative AI into its core consumer products.
